memos.headline: S08 at 52-week high leads momentum; S02 and S07 show deteriorating relative strength
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market today. S08 is sitting at its 52-week high with +8.4% 4-week return, +12.4% 12-week relative strength vs SPY, and RSI at 65.7—strong but not yet overbought. S04 is similarly powerful with +34.3% over 12 weeks and +30.9% relative strength, though its +8.5% premium to the 50-day mean makes me slightly cautious on entry timing. On the weak side, S02 has broken down badly: RSI 39.9, -11.7% over 12 weeks, -15.1% relative strength, and trading 5.7% below its 50-day mean—this is a name I want to avoid until it reclaims the 50-day. S07 is 22.8% off its high with the worst 12-week relative strength in the universe at -20.6%, and while it has stabilized near the 50-day, I see no reason to step in front of that kind of damage until price proves otherwise above roughly 850.

views.note: At 52-week high with strong momentum across all timeframes and +12.4% 12w relative strength; would reassess on a close below 320 (roughly the 50-day area).
Exceptional 12-week return of +34.3% and +30.9% relative strength, but +8.5% above 50d mean suggests a pullback toward 475 would be a better entry; still constructive.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Extraordinary Earnings Power; S09 and S01 Flash Warning Signs on Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between names with durable, expanding earnings power and those suffering margin erosion. S10 stands out with 106% YoY revenue growth, a 62% net margin, and $59.69B in net income on only $33.37B of total debt—this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group. S05 is similarly exceptional: 93.7% net margin, 24% revenue growth, near-negligible debt at $14.79B, and net income up nearly 4x YoY. On the other end, S09 posted just 4.9% net margin with net income down 46% YoY on anemic 2.4% revenue growth, and S01 saw net income decline 16% YoY on only 1.5% revenue growth with a 14.4% margin and $29.30B in debt against $21.20B in revenue. I would need to see S09's margin stabilize above 7% and S01's revenue re-accelerate above mid-single digits before reconsidering either name.

views.note: 106% revenue growth, 62% net margin, and modest $33.37B debt make this the best fundamental story in the universe.
93.7% net margin and nearly 4x YoY net income growth with minimal leverage ($14.79B debt) signal extraordinary earnings durability.
39.7% net margin, 17.7% revenue growth, and 31.3% net income growth with manageable $40.29B debt reflect strong, consistent earnings power.
$200.61B revenue with 19.6% growth and 245% net income expansion are compelling, though $133B debt and 31.2% margin warrant monitoring.
24% revenue growth and 65% net income growth with a 17.5% margin show improving fundamentals, but $36.21B debt on $20.54B revenue is elevated.
27.7% revenue growth and 36.9% margin are solid, but $460.52B in total debt is an outsized liability that could compress equity returns if rates stay high.
16.4% revenue growth and 27.2% margin are respectable but lag peers, and $82.30B debt is meaningful relative to earnings.
Flat 0.4% revenue growth and a thin 4.9% margin leave little room for error despite 61% net income improvement off a low base.
Net income fell 46% YoY to $4.18B on a 4.9% margin with only 2.4% revenue growth—clear earnings deterioration.
Revenue grew just 1.5% while net income declined 15.8%, and $29.30B debt exceeds annual revenue of $21.20B, signaling strained fundamentals.

memos.headline: Rising Yields and Sticky Inflation Point to a Hawkish Pause — Favor Banks and Staples Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see a regime that has shifted from easing to a hawkish pause: the Fed raised the upper bound 25bp over the past three months to 4.00%, reversing the prior easing cycle, while 12-month headline CPI is running at 3.4% — well above target. The 10-year yield has surged 77bp in three months to 5.17%, a punishing move for anything with duration, and the 10y-2y spread has flattened 28bp year-over-year to just 31bp, consistent with a late-cycle tightening bias. The labor market remains firm at 4.1% unemployment (down 20bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons), which gives the Fed cover to keep rates elevated. My base case is rates stay at or above 4% through year-end; a CPI print falling below 3% or unemployment rising above 4.4% would flip me toward an easing call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth names face severe headwinds with the 10y at 5.17% and rising; multiples should compress further.
Banks benefit from a hawkish pause with a positively sloped curve (31bp 10y-2y) and firm loan demand in a 4.1% unemployment economy.
Staples offer defensive carry in a high-rate, sticky-inflation environment where real consumer spending is under pressure.
Cyclicals are caught between a solid labor market and tightening financial conditions; I lack conviction either way until the next payroll print.
High-duration growth is the most exposed sector to the 99bp 12-month rise in the 10y yield; avoid until rates stabilize.
Energy benefits from nominal GDP resilience but faces demand risk if the hawkish pause tips growth; staying neutral.

memos.headline: S10 and S07 Show Positive Event-Driven Momentum; S08 and S03 Face Leadership Uncertainty
memos.body: I see the clearest positive narrative shifts in S10 and S07, both of which posted strong price reactions to earnings disclosures (+8.7% and +5.6% respectively) and followed up with material agreements suggesting operational momentum. S10 in particular has had three 8-K filings in six weeks—a new financing agreement, a strong earnings print, and an Other Events disclosure—indicating a company in active deal mode with market validation. S08 and S03 both disclosed director/officer departures or appointments, which introduces governance uncertainty that media tone typically turns negative on before stabilizing. S04, S02, and S05 had routine Reg FD or Other Events filings with no observable price reaction data, leaving me with low conviction on narrative direction for those names. I would lean into the momentum stories where tone has turned decisively positive and stay cautious on the leadership-change names until the dust settles.

views.note: Three material filings in six weeks including an earnings beat with +8.7% price reaction and new financing signal a strong positive narrative shift.
Earnings-driven +5.6% pop in early August followed by a material definitive agreement in September suggests sustained positive sentiment momentum.
Director/officer departure via 8-K/A typically generates negative media tone and governance uncertainty that may not yet be fully priced.
Two filings in a week including a leadership change and an Other Events disclosure suggest potential instability; tone likely turning cautious.
Single Reg FD disclosure with no price reaction data provides insufficient signal to form a directional sentiment view.
Routine Reg FD filing with no observable market reaction; no narrative shift detected.
Other Events filing from mid-August with no price data; insufficient evidence of a tone change.

memos.headline: Surging Oil Prices Signal Geopolitical Supply Risk; Policy Uncertainty Fading but Energy Exposure Demands Caution
memos.body: I am focused on the 34% three-month surge in WTI to $95.88/bbl, which is the dominant geopolitical signal in today's data — this magnitude of move typically reflects supply disruption or sanctions-related tightening rather than pure demand. At the same time, the Economic Policy Uncertainty index has dropped nearly 40% over three months to 279, and VIX is down to 15.67, suggesting markets are pricing out broad policy tail risk even as energy markets flash red. HY spreads remain benign at 2.80% but have widened 11bp over the past month, hinting that credit is beginning to notice the oil cost pass-through. I have moderate conviction that energy-exposed names benefit structurally from this supply backdrop, while names with high energy-input costs or China-linked supply chains face margin pressure until we see either a diplomatic resolution or an SPR release that breaks the crude rally. A reversal in WTI below $80 or new export-control escalation against China would change my positioning.

views.note: Recent 8-K (Other Events) lacks detail to assess geopolitical exposure; holding neutral until clarity on whether the filing relates to supply-chain or regulatory matters.
Two 8-K filings in quick succession (Reg FD + Other Events) suggest proactive disclosure, and if S10 has energy-sector exposure the crude rally is a structural tailwind.
Reg FD disclosure on Sep 2 is uninformative on geopolitical risk; benign VIX and falling policy uncertainty keep me sidelined rather than negative.
With WTI up 34% in three months and HY OAS widening, any name with high energy-input costs or tight margins faces headwinds; S05's Aug 8-K (Other Events) does not dispel that concern.
Reg FD filing on Sep 8 is opaque; declining policy uncertainty is mildly supportive but the oil-cost shock keeps me from going long without more information.
Early-August Reg FD disclosure is stale; no subsequent filings and no clear geopolitical catalyst either way.
